title: Competitive Signal Lexicon & Priority Grid for Model Landscape
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a defensible, operational lexicon that translates heterogeneous external signals (e.g., new open checkpoints, quantization reports, latency benchmarks, outage events, supplier commercial changes) into a compact priority grid and procurement trigger index for PM + sales. The goal is a repeatable mapping that non-experts can use to decide: (A) whether to onboard a model variant, (B) which region/capacity to provision, and (C) whether to escalate to sales/finance for reserved capacity negotiations.
background: We have many informal sources (Slack scouts, PRs, benchmark spreadsheets, partner alerts) producing noisy signals. PMs and Solutions Eng spend ad hoc effort synthesizing this into decisions. Existing artifacts (model watchlists, supply-readiness ledgers) are useful but inconsistent: different teams weight latency vs. cost vs. availability differently. This ticket scopes a canonical lexicon + scoring rubric and a simple 3x3 priority grid to surface top 10 candidate model actions weekly.
proposed_solution: Deliver a CSV-friendly lexicon and a lightweight scoring script (pseudo-code) that maps signal types to normalized scores across axes: Performance, Availability, Commercial Risk, Integration Effort, and Strategic Fit. Combine axis scores into a procurement-trigger index with clear thresholds for: 'Investigate', 'Trial (Dedicated)', 'Negotiate Reserved', 'Monitor Only'. Produce a one-page priority grid and a reproducible weekly snapshot job (owned by PM) that emits top candidates and rationales.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable lexicon (CSV) with at least 18 signal types and normalization guidance
A scoring rubric with example calculations for three historical model events (at least one positive adoption, one fallback, one degradation)
A 3x3 priority grid PDF and an example weekly snapshot (CSV) produced from existing signals
Stakeholder review sign-off from Eng (runtime lead) and Sales Ops
An onboarding doc for Solutions Eng to interpret grid outputs and run the snapshot locally
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs. fidelity: a compact lexicon reduces cognitive load but may hide edge cases (e.g., quant pipeline incompatibility)
Automated scoring risks false positives; require human verification for 'Negotiate Reserved' tier
Scope vs. speed: prototype limited to top-of-funnel signals (public model releases, pricing updates, latency incidents) — proprietary partner signals are out-of-scope for the first iteration
tasks: Inventory current signal sources (Drive spreadsheets, Slack watch channel, GitHub issues, partner feeds)
Draft lexicon CSV with fields: signal_id, signal_type, description, measurement_fn, normalization_range, weight_hint
Define axis weights and threshold buckets; create pseudo-code scoring notebook
Run scoring on historical events (Q4 2025 dataset) and produce three case studies
Create priority-grid visual (3x3) and one-pager playbook
Publish snapshot job and run first weekly export; add to PM dashboard (link)
